neighbours.label: molecular-genetics research prose: the function word after 'used as' or 'one of' when a gene, protein or cell line is given its role (used as [a] marker for, one of [the] most commonly mutated genes)
fire: The surface protein CD34 has been used as a marker for blood stem cells.
The enzyme telomerase is one of the most commonly activated genes in human tumours.
The transcription factor Nanog is widely used as a marker for pluripotent cells.
The gene TP53 is one of the most frequently mutated genes in human cancers.
The antigen Ki-67 has long been used as a marker for dividing cells.
The oncogene KRAS is one of the most commonly altered genes in pancreatic cancer.
The protein GFAP has been used as a key marker for astrocytes in the brain.
The gene BRCA1 is one of the most thoroughly studied genes in breast cancer.
quiet: The old church tower has been used as a landmark for fishing boats.
The village square is one of the most commonly photographed places in the county.
The red flag is widely used as a warning for swimmers.
The harbour bridge is one of the most frequently repaired roads in the region.
The oak bench has long been used as a meeting point for walkers.
The night train is one of the most commonly delayed services in the country.
The blue ribbon has been used as a key prize for bakers at the fair.
The coast path is one of the most thoroughly mapped routes in the north.
